title: The war in Ukraine explained
subtitle: Since February 24, 2022
subject: comprendreLeMonde
description: An invasion meant to last three days became the largest war in Europe since 1945. A look at the causes and the consequences of the conflict in **Ukraine**.

hero.hook: A lightning offensive meant to last three days turned into the biggest war Europe has seen since 1945.

blocks.text: On February 24, 2022, Russia launched a massive military offensive against **Ukraine**, starting the most destructive conflict on European soil since 1945. Nothing about it was sudden. It was the outcome of tensions that had been building for decades over Ukrainian sovereignty.

sections.title: The post-Soviet legacy and a clash of identities

blocks.text: The roots of the war go back to the breakup of the USSR in 1991. Part of the Russian elite, Vladimir Putin among them, experienced Ukrainian independence as the amputation of Russia's historic heart, and refused to see Ukraine as a fully sovereign nation.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky voiced Paddington Bear in the Ukrainian version of the film, a nod to his acting career before politics.

Ukraine held the world's third-largest nuclear arsenal in 1991, and chose to disarm. Under the **[[Budapest Memorandum (1994)]]**, it traded its warheads for guarantees of its territorial integrity. But its move closer to the EU and NATO looked to the Kremlin like hostile encirclement.

The final break came in 2014, when Ukrainians drove out a pro-Russian president during the Maidan revolution. Russia responded by illegally annexing Crimea and backing an armed insurgency in the **[[Donbas and the separatist republics]]** of eastern Ukraine. That conflict stayed frozen for eight years, and it became the laboratory for the full-scale war of 2022.

On February 24, 2022, the Russian army attacked on several fronts. Moscow wanted to topple the government in Kyiv within days. That ambition rested on one huge mistake: it underestimated Ukrainian national unity, and how far the Ukrainian army had modernized since 2014.

blocks.caption: The Russian invasion of February 2022 caused heavy destruction in many Ukrainian cities

blocks.text: President Volodymyr Zelensky turned down the evacuation the United States offered him, saying: “I need ammunition, not a ride.” Through his daily messages he became the symbol of a nation that refused to bend.

The battle of Kyiv ended in a stinging Russian failure in the spring of 2022. Facing a mobile Ukrainian resistance armed with Western weapons, Moscow pulled its troops out of the north to concentrate on the east and the south. The conflict turned into a war of attrition, along a front line more than 1,000 kilometers long.

sections.title: A global economic and security earthquake

blocks.text: The shock wave from the invasion went far beyond Ukraine's borders. Western powers rolled out an unprecedented set of sanctions to paralyze the Russian war machine: shutting Russian banks out of the **[[SWIFT]]** system and freezing the central bank's reserves marked a historic break. Those measures also upended energy flows, and Europe had to move fast away from Russian gas, which had covered 40% of its needs.
At the start of the war, the Ukrainian government updated its “Diia” app so that citizens could report the position of Russian tanks in real time.

Farming was the other big casualty. Ukraine, known as “the breadbasket of Europe,” saw its ports blockaded, which threatened famine in countries that depend on its grain. The war also welded the Atlantic Alliance back together, pushing Finland and Sweden to join NATO.

After more than two years of fighting, the war has become a high-intensity conflict in which drones and satellites sit alongside trench methods from another century. The failure of the Ukrainian counter-offensives of 2023 showed how hard ground has become to win back, between minefields and constant surveillance of the battlefield.

blocks.caption: Western military support for Ukraine, channeled through NATO, grew steadily as the war went on

blocks.text: The question now is industrial endurance. Russia has shifted its economy onto a total war footing, while Ukraine depends on Western military and financial aid continuing to arrive.

blocks.text: Ukrainian resistance turned a lightning invasion meant to last three days into a global war of attrition, one that has redrawn the alliances left over from the Cold War and shaken world energy and food security.
